data.narrative:
Paradromics is a Series B biotech company founded by Matt Angle with co-founders Edmund Huber and Andreas Schaefer. The company has raised approximately $90–120M in dilutive capital plus ~$18M in non-dilutive NIH/DARPA funding. The valuation analysis draws from a peer universe of 3 public comps (RXRX, TEM, ONT.L) and 8 private-stage companies in Biotech & Health, including Colossal Biosciences, Chai Discovery, and New Limit.

Two triangulation methods are applicable. Stage-progression analysis, using the $90M raised proxy as a base, applies a 1.9x step-up multiplier typical of Series B to next-stage progression, yielding $171M. Peer-median analysis across three same-sector, same/adjacent-stage private comparables yields a median valuation of $3.8B, with a range of $3.1B–$10.3B. Public-comp anchoring via P/S multiple (7.4x median across the three public tickers) cannot be applied due to absence of disclosed revenue for the private target.

The triangulated analysis supports a valuation range of $145M (low) to $4.4B (high), with a median of $2.0B. The wide spread reflects material uncertainty: stage-progression implies significant upside from current raised capital, while peer-median is anchored to later-stage (Series C) comparables. Key sensitivities include the applicability of Series C peer valuations to a Series B company and the degree to which non-dilutive funding should adjust the raised-capital proxy.
